summary: Feed s105_single to NDR is degraded due to tool overload: 14.58 Gbps microbursts exceed the 10 Gbps tool port (146% capacity, 2 intervals over 80% threshold). All other checks (duplicates, encryption, VLANs, one-way, drops) are healthy.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is aggregating too much traffic onto a single 10 Gbps NDR egress without load balancing or burst handling. 1ms microbursts peaked at 14.58 Gbps (146% of port capacity, metric 1.458 vs 0.8 threshold) across 2 intervals, exceeding the NDR's line-rate and buffer capacity.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR ingress will drop packets during bursts due to port oversubscription. Even though packet_drops check is currently healthy, sustained microbursts cause incomplete flows, failed reassembly and missed detections - directly undermining NDR which requires both directions and full payload at 10 Gbps.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute traffic across 2x10 Gbps tool ports with 5-tuple hashing to keep flows intact and keep per-port utilization below 80% even during 14.58 Gbps bursts, preserving full payload and bidirectional visibility required by NDR. Alternative is filter/slice but that would reduce detection coverage.
